take_homes: Start from the teammate's job and their current way of doing it, not from what I built. Then pick one of the four sharing strategies by the outcome it moves.
Write the people plan with names for who owns, governs and operates the thing. A technical plan next to unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
Talk to one person about how they do the job today before building anything more, and test what would have to be true for them to switch.

monday.move: Talk to one pricing working group member about how they pull usage data into their pricing analysis today. Ask the question from monday.md and run the first test on whether the pilot-cohort brief appears where they already look.
monday.who: The pricing working group analyst who currently builds the usage view by hand
monday.when: Monday morning, 30 minutes before my team stand-up
monday.stop_condition: If they say they would not stop using their spreadsheet, I stop building the brief for them and drop that candidate.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so the people plan needs an owner for that before anyone else can build on mine.

misconception.why: The module never taught prompting, and the whole outcome was a people plan with named owners. That made me doubt that better prompts are the skill. I'm not convinced yet, because the prompts are what produced the files.

one_line: Useful if you're about to roll something out to a team. It made me name who owns it and talk to one person first, though the switch question comes up three times.
